verdict.line: You lose extended trades from level 3 to 8 against his Q/W sustain loop, but the lane evens out once Shadow Dash and your core items come online near level 9, matching the overall 49.8% win rate over 1784 games.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's early game revolves around spamming Q (Obliterate) at range 675 every 8/7/6/5/4 seconds — dealing increased damage if it only hits you — and banking that damage into W (Indestructible) to shield and heal himself, so this lane is a resource war you cannot win by trading evenly. Shen's only way to not bleed health is to eat that Q with W (Feint) or decline the trade outright, re-engaging only when Ki Strike is ready for the free empowered auto. The close 49.8% win rate reflects this: it's even on average because Shen's teleport-level map presence recovers what's lost in lane, not because the 1v1 itself is comfortable.

theirWindow.when: Q (Obliterate) is up and he pushes
theirWindow.what: He'll smash for max single-target damage and immediately bank it into W (Indestructible) to shield up. Don't stand and trade here — block it with Feint or step outside range 675.

yourWindow.when: his Q is down and Ki Strike is ready
yourWindow.what: Step into range 475 and land Q (Vorpal Blade) with an empowered auto to life-tap the healing back. This is the only trade you actually win before your items come online.

start.why: Highest-winrate start (49.2% over 1304 games); the on-hit regen directly offsets the chip damage from his Q poke pattern.

boots.why: Most-picked boots (68.4% pick, 49.1% WR); the magic resist blunts both Q damage and the extended trades he's fishing for.

core.why: Most-picked first core item — the HP scaling and wave-clear let you win the siege instead of fighting him in melee range.
Second item in every top build path; keeps you alive through the skirmishes that start once teamfights open up.
Best-performing third item (65.5% over 87 games); the shield directly answers his burst from Q and Death's Grasp.

situational.when: the team needs grievous wounds to shut down his W self-heal
you're getting poked down early and need sustain before finishing your first core item
the enemy team stacks other sustained-damage threats alongside him
the game goes long and you want raw HP for split-push durability

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustain and scaling health through a long poke-and-attrition lane is exactly what you need against a champion trying to win that exact war.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the best winrate of the three real pages (48.7% over 30.1% pick) and lets you reset the wave you're losing in lane; Flash alone also dodges Death's Grasp. Flash+Ignite is the more common pick (64.8%) if you want earlier pressure instead.

playing.title: Hold Feint for Q
playing.detail: Save W (Feint) for his Q (Obliterate) walk-up poke instead of using it reactively mid-fight; it absorbs the hit fully and denies the shield he'd bank off it.

playing.title: Trade only on Ki Strike
playing.detail: Only step into Q (Vorpal Blade) range 475 when your passive empowered auto is up — without it you lose the damage race to his Q/W loop.

playing.title: Respect Shadow Dash's real use
playing.detail: Shadow Dash taunts enemy champions it passes through and deals minor damage on cooldown 16/14/12/10/8s — use it to force an engage when his Q is down, not as an escape, since it doesn't disengage you.

playing.title: Play around level 6 carefully
playing.detail: Once he hits 6, don't commit below 50% HP in extended trades; Realm of Death drags you into his dimension and steals your stats if he wins the fight.

playing.title: Don't clump for Death's Grasp
playing.detail: Death's Grasp pulls all enemies in its area at range 700 — stay at minion-clear spacing so you're not the only target it can reach, especially from level 6-8.

playing.title: Siege instead of skirmish
playing.detail: From level 9 on, use your Titanic Hydra wave-clear to push minions into towers rather than matching him fight for fight.

playing.title: Win the game off Stand United
playing.detail: Your win condition is global — once Stand United is up, shield and teleport into a winning fight elsewhere rather than forcing something in a lane he's favored in.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win rates are pulled from measured Shen vs. Mordekaiser games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Try to use Shen’s [P] to absorb Mordekaiser’s (Q) while engaging. Be careful of Mordekaiser’s (R) after reaching level 6 by keeping an eye out on your health.
